definition: A way to split one physical network into separate logical networks.
exampleSentence: We put the guest Wi-Fi on its own VLAN so visitors cannot reach internal servers.

definition: A short notation such as 10.0.0.0/24 that describes a block of IP addresses.
exampleSentence: The firewall rule allows the whole office range written in CIDR notation as 10.20.0.0/16.

definition: A method that lets many private devices share one public IP address.
exampleSentence: The router uses NAT so all our laptops can reach the internet through one address.

definition: The routing protocol that exchanges routes between large networks on the internet.
exampleSentence: A wrong BGP announcement sent part of the internet traffic to the wrong country.

turkish: önce en kısa yolu aç protokolü
definition: A routing protocol that finds the shortest path inside one company network.
exampleSentence: Our core switches use OSPF to learn the best route between office buildings.

definition: The largest packet size that a network link can send without splitting it.
exampleSentence: The VPN was slow because the MTU was too large and packets kept being fragmented.

definition: Rules that give important traffic, such as voice calls, priority on the network.
exampleSentence: We enabled QoS so video meetings do not stutter when someone downloads a big file.

definition: A separate network area for servers that must be reachable from the internet.
exampleSentence: The public web server sits in the DMZ, away from our internal file servers.

definition: A system that watches network traffic and raises an alert when it sees an attack.
exampleSentence: The IDS flagged hundreds of strange login attempts coming from a single address.

definition: A system that not only detects attacks but also blocks them automatically.
exampleSentence: After we turned on the IPS, known exploit traffic was dropped before reaching our servers.

definition: A firewall that filters HTTP traffic to protect a website from common attacks.
exampleSentence: The WAF blocked a SQL injection attempt against our login page last night.

definition: An XML standard that lets one system tell another that a user is already signed in.
exampleSentence: Our HR portal uses SAML so employees sign in with their company account.

definition: A standard that lets an app access your data without knowing your password.
exampleSentence: The calendar app asked for OAuth permission before reading my meetings.

definition: A layer on top of OAuth that tells an app who the signed-in user is.
exampleSentence: We replaced the old login form with OIDC so users can sign in with their work account.

definition: A protocol for searching and reading user information stored in a directory.
exampleSentence: The VPN checks the username and password against our LDAP server.

definition: A system where permissions are given to roles instead of single people.
exampleSentence: With RBAC, a new support engineer gets the right access just by joining the team.

definition: Tools and rules that control and record the use of powerful admin accounts.
exampleSentence: Admins must check out the root password from the PAM tool and every session is recorded.

definition: Software that lets a company configure, secure and wipe employee phones remotely.
exampleSentence: When Ayşe lost her phone, we used MDM to wipe all company data from it.

turkish: güvenlik olayı toplama ve analiz sistemi
definition: A platform that collects logs from many systems and finds suspicious patterns.
exampleSentence: The SIEM linked a failed VPN login with an odd file download and created one alert.

definition: Software on laptops and servers that spots attacks and helps the team respond.
exampleSentence: The EDR isolated the infected laptop from the network within seconds.

definition: A public ID number given to a known security vulnerability.
exampleSentence: Please check whether our servers are affected by the new CVE published this morning.

definition: Clues, such as strange files or IP addresses, that show a system may be hacked.
exampleSentence: The security team shared a list of IOC values so we could search our logs for them.

definition: A design that uses separate models for writing data and for reading data.
exampleSentence: We adopted CQRS so the busy reporting queries no longer slow down order creation.

fullForm: Single responsibility, Open-closed, Liskov, Interface segregation, Dependency inversion
definition: Five design principles that help developers write code that is easy to change.
exampleSentence: The reviewer said this class breaks SOLID because it handles payments and also sends emails.

definition: The amount of time a piece of data may be kept before it expires.
exampleSentence: We set the TTL of the cache entry to five minutes so prices stay fresh.

definition: A measured number, such as success rate, that shows how well a service performs.
exampleSentence: Our main SLI is the percentage of requests that finish in under 300 milliseconds.

definition: A target value for an SLI that the team promises to reach.
exampleSentence: Our SLO says the API must be available 99.9 percent of the time each month.

definition: A small signed token that proves who the user is when calling an API.
exampleSentence: The mobile app sends a JWT in the header of every request to the backend.

definition: An attack where a hacker makes a website run malicious script in a visitor's browser.
exampleSentence: The comment form was vulnerable to XSS because it displayed user input without cleaning it.

definition: An attack that tricks a logged-in user's browser into sending an unwanted request.
exampleSentence: We added a hidden token to every form to protect the site against CSRF.

fullForm: Open Worldwide Application Security Project Top 10
turkish: en yaygın web güvenlik riskleri listesi
definition: A well-known list of the ten most serious security risks for web applications.
exampleSentence: Our security training explains each risk in the OWASP Top 10 with a real example.

definition: A fast dedicated network that connects servers to shared storage devices.
exampleSentence: The database servers read their disks from the SAN instead of using local drives.

definition: A list of rules that says who or what is allowed to use a resource.
exampleSentence: We updated the ACL on the shared folder so only the finance team can open it.

definition: The system of certificates and keys that lets computers trust each other.
exampleSentence: Our internal PKI issues a certificate to every laptop that joins the company network.

definition: Tools that stop sensitive data from leaving the company by mistake or on purpose.
exampleSentence: The DLP policy blocked an email that contained a list of customer credit card numbers.

definition: A platform that automates the steps of handling security alerts.
exampleSentence: With SOAR, a phishing report now deletes the email from every inbox automatically.

definition: A complete list of all the components and libraries inside a piece of software.
exampleSentence: The customer asked us to send an SBOM so they can check our libraries for known risks.

definition: Managing servers and networks with code files instead of clicking in a console.
exampleSentence: Thanks to IaC, we can rebuild the whole test environment with a single command.

definition: Scanning source code for security problems without running the program.
exampleSentence: The pipeline runs SAST on every pull request and fails if it finds a serious issue.

definition: A platform that combines alerts from endpoints, email, network and cloud into one view.
exampleSentence: The XDR connected a suspicious email with a strange login and a file download in one incident.
